transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-07 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Evan (Redwood SE), Sara (Redwood CSM), Priya (Jasperio Head of Search), Liam (ML Eng), Olivia (CTO), Noah (PM)

Summary:
Quick hosted API walkthrough of embeddings + reranker endpoints, discuss pilot scope, performance targets, data security questions (KMS, SSO), and pilot logistics. Customer wants a 2-week pilot to compare Redwood hosted reranking against their current hybrid BM25+vector stack.

Topics:
- Hosted embeddings endpoint: dimensionality, batching, cost per embedding, rate limits
- Reranker endpoint: pairwise vs pointwise scoring, streaming, latency SLOs
- Console: workloads, traced requests, TTL cache stats and token cost breakdown
- Pilot logistics: datasets, success metrics (p@5, latency 99th percentile < 200ms), contract and SOW

Action items called out at end (see metadata)

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: alright hi everyone thanks for joining on time, I'm Maya from Redwood, i'll kick off, we've got Evan our SE and Sara from success. Priya, thanks for setting this up
[00:10] Priya: yeah thanks Maya, excited to see how the hosted API could fit into Jasperio search, we've been battling tail latency and embedding drift with our in-house vector service
[00:18] Evan: cool, quick agenda, show embeddings endpoint, then reranker demo, then console observability and then open planning for pilot. sound good?
[00:25] Priya: yes
[00:27] Liam: quick note — we'll care a lot about 99th perc latency and token cost. also our docs are long; many docs exceed 5k tokens sometimes, so interested in sequence handling and kv cache behavior
[00:36] Evan: good call. on hosted we do chunking guidance and KV cache for chat-ish flows, for search rerank the typical approach is embedding first then a lightweight rerank model — you can pin model variants. the reranker endpoint accepts a candidate list and returns scores/ordering, and it can run as a pointwise model or pairwise depending on your config
[00:55] Noah: pairwise meaning you score pairs and compare?
[00:58] Evan: yes, pairwise ranking compares candidate pairs which tends to be more robust for small candidate sets, but it's heavier. pointwise gives a score per doc independently; lower compute but sometimes lower ranking quality. we often recommend pointwise with a small transformer reranker for speed on hosted.
[01:15] Priya: what kind of latency are we talking about for rerank? 100ms per request?
[01:19] Evan: it depends — for a 10-candidate rerank with our optimized runtime on an A100-backed hosted instance you can see ~60-120ms P50, P95 often under 200ms. Keep in mind if you enable big context or long doc rerank it'll add time. Also we have batching windows that can reduce cost but add a ms or two; you can configure strict latency SLOs to prefer immediate execution.
[01:40] Olivia: security — we need to know about encryption and key management. we use GCP KMS for keys today. can Redwood integrate with that or do we need to use Redwood-managed keys?
[01:50] Sara: yes we support customer KMS integrations for Private and Dedicated, for hosted we offer Bring Your Own Key via an encrypted channel, and we can provide the SOC2 artefact and an ISO checklist. we'll attach the security pack in follow up.
[02:05] Priya: perfect. also about data retention — can we set short TTLs for embedding caches? we don't want derivative artifacts stored long term
[02:12] Evan: yes TTLs are configurable per-customer, and prefix caching is opt-in for hosted. note that caching reduces calls to the reranker and cost per token significantly. there is also an option to disable persistent KV cache entirely if required.
[02:26] Liam: on embeddings — what's the vector dimension and can you return raw float vectors? we currently use 1536-d vectors
[02:33] Evan: we support configurable model choices — many of default open models use 1k–2k dims; our API will return floats as base64 or JSON arrays depending on SDK. For cost, you can quantize (8-bit) for storage in the console, but we send float for live responses; we also have a quantized storage path if you want to save tokens.
[02:50] Priya: hmm do we need to change our similarity pipeline? currently BM25 produces candidates then we score with dot product on our FAISS cluster, then a small transformer rerank near-RTB
[02:59] Evan: that pattern aligns well. typical pilot is: 1) use hosted embeddings in place of your vector encoder to evaluate vector quality, 2) optionally use hosted reranker to replace the local transformer rerank, and 3) measure latency/cost. many customers keep FAISS for vector lookup and use Redwood for rerank to reduce infra overhead.
[03:15] Maya: i want to demo a short flow, i'll share my screen and run an embedding request and then a rerank call — you'll see request/response and how it appears in the console.
[03:25] [screen share noise]
[03:30] Evan: here's the embeddings call — example: POST /v1/embeddings with model param, a batch of 64 texts, we show tokens consumed and cost breakdown. note the batch size controls throughput; our optimizer (Optimize) can recommend batching sizes based on latencies.
[03:44] Priya: the batched 64 — is that on the client side or server will buffer?
[03:47] Evan: client batching. server supports concurrent small batches and also has an internal batching window for micro-requests. client-side recommended batch sizes are in our SDK.
[03:56] Liam: do you support streaming from reranker so we can get partial scores?
[04:00] Evan: reranker returns a final scoring payload; we do support streaming for generation endpoints, but scoring is usually atomic. for very large sets we provide chunked scoring APIs.
[04:10] Priya: one of our concerns is cold start latency when model is idle overnight — does hosted keep warm instances?
[04:16] Evan: yes we have warm pool options for Dedicated, and for hosted we keep hot instances for active customers; if your QPS is very low there may be occasional slightly higher latencies at first request but we can set keep-alives for pilot.
[04:28] Noah: okay demo looks good. can you show the console trace for a rerank call?
[04:32] [screen tap]
[04:35] Evan: here, request trace: you get the end-to-end token cost, model name, exact latency percentiles, and a score breakdown for rerank if you enable explainability. the explainability shows token-level attention proxies, which is approximate.
[04:50] Priya: explainability is useful. can we capture drift metrics over time?
[04:54] Sara: yes Optimize has a quality-monitoring feature where you can upload a golden set and get regression alerts tied to prompt sets — we'll set that up for pilot.
[05:05] Liam: about pricing — do you do per-embedding plus per-rerank request? we need rough numbers to model cost against our current infra
[05:12] Maya: yes typical hosted pricing is per-1k embeddings + per-100 rerank requests; we'll send the pricing sheet after the call. for pilots we can propose credits or short-term discounts depending on scope.
[05:22] Olivia: need to confirm compliance for enterprise procurement — do you have SAML SSO and RBAC?
[05:27] Sara: yes SAML SSO and fine-grained RBAC on Console, and audit logs are available as part of enterprise bundle. we'll attach the SAML integration guide.
[05:38] Priya: great. some technical questions from Liam — do you keep raw logs of input text for hosted?
[05:43] Evan: by default Redwood stores data for 30 days for observability; for enterprise you can set zero retention or have encrypted forwarding to your storage. Hosted has an option to opt out of data retention entirely.
[05:56] Liam: for evaluation we want to run a batch of 10k queries: embedding + rerank. what's the fastest way to get accurate cost numbers?
[06:03] Evan: send the sample data and we'll run a pilot harness with identical candidate sizes; we'll report P50/P95 latencies and cost per query. that's part of the pilot scope we usually propose.
[06:12] Priya: success metrics — we want p@5 increase of at least 6% and 99th perc latency under 200ms. is that realistic?
[06:20] Evan: that's realistic to test in a pilot. quality improvements depend on dataset but many customers see 3–10% gains with our reranker models. we can also tune model variants and quantization settings.
[06:32] Maya: ok logistics — here's proposed pilot timeline: Week 0: contract + data share, Week 1: baseline runs and embedding comparison, Week 2: rerank trial and tuning, Week 3: results, decision.
[06:45] Noah: timeline is tight but possible. procurement needs a demo of security docs before legal signs.
[06:50] Maya: we'll prioritize security docs in the follow-up email.
[06:55] [long pause as demo continues showing console charts]
[07:10] Evan: demo note — we ran a sample rerank with a 12-candidate list, P95 ~ 180ms; here's the console trace and you can export raw timings. Link: https://redwood.app/console/demo/jasperio-sample (demo link, restricted)
[07:30] Priya: can we run A/B tests where we fallback to our local reranker on failure? we want graceful degradation
[07:36] Evan: yes routing policies can be set — traffic split or automatic fallback if hosted responds > threshold. console will show rollouts and canary results.
[07:47] Liam: any mentioning of model drift detection — can you alert if embedding similarity drops across nightly batches?
[07:52] Sara: yes Optimize monitors embed distribution stats and can trigger regression alerts if drift passes a threshold. we can tie alerts into Slack or PagerDuty.
[08:05] Priya: ok procurement question re: data residency — we need EU-only hosting for EU customers
[08:11] Evan: we have region pinning and EU-hosted endpoints; for Private deployments we support full on-prem.
[08:20] Olivia: with hosted pilot we still worry about access controls — can Redwood give us an IP allowlist and VPC peering?
[08:27] Sara: for hosted we support IP allowlist and private link options depending on cloud provider. VPC peering is available for Dedicated; for hosted we can do private routes with our partner providers.
[08:39] Priya: also curious about model updates — if you upgrade a reranker model will results change? how do we reproduce prior behavior?
[08:46] Evan: we support model pinning to a specific version. console shows model lineage and you can request a rollback. also we provide seed and eval sets so you can reproduce runs.
[08:58] Noah: sounds good. any competitors we should be aware of? we looked at Algolia's hybrid and OpenSearch vector plugin but they lack managed reranker suggestions
[09:05] Maya: yep some folks build in-house rerankers but that's operationally heavy; Redwood reduces that burden.
[09:12] Priya: last question — can we run sample code in our environment and keep keys ephemeral?
[09:16] Evan: yes we provide SDKs and ephemeral API keys for test runs, and we can rotate keys automatically.
[09:23] Priya: ok that's it from our side, thanks for the clear demo.
[09:27] Maya: thanks all — recapping next steps: i'll send SOW and pricing, Evan will set up test harness once you share data, Liam will upload queries and docs, we'll schedule the benchmark week of 2026-07-20.
[09:40] Olivia: sounds good. we'll review security docs and aim to sign pilot SOW the week after.
[09:45] Maya: great, we'll follow up in email; thank you everyone.

End of transcript.
